Subject: POC trial: model selection & success criteria

Hi Alex —

Great to chat earlier. Quick recap from our discovery and a proposed plan for the POC trial so we can align on scope, ownership, and success criteria. I left the technical details to Aditya below but wanted to capture the sales/pm view first.

Recap / goals
- Primary goal: evaluate model quality for customer-facing answers in our account aggregation product (balance reconciliation, transaction categorization, concise explainers).
- Data characteristics: mostly English (~75%), Spanish (~15%), Portuguese (~5%) and some short merchant names/non-English tokens.
- Latency target (interactive flows): p95 < 350ms for single-request queries; throughput target for background batch scoring: 50 qps.

Proposed POC plan (3 weeks)
- Week 0 (this week): finalize scope, sample dataset (500-1,000 queries across languages), and success criteria.
- Week 1: deploy trial models, run initial evaluation on the sample set, tune prompts.
- Week 2: run extended evaluation (50k synthetic + replayed traffic), measure latency/cost/regression, and collect human evals.
- Deliverable: evaluation report with model recommendations and recommended production config.

Success criteria (suggested)
- Quality: >= 88% pass rate on domain-specific correctness checks (per evaluation_template.xlsx).
- Latency: p95 endpoint < 350ms (US-west).
- Cost: token cost not to exceed our target (we'll share numbers in the POC).
- Multilingual coverage: Spanish and Portuguese accuracy within 10 points of English baseline.

Model selection (initial candidates)
- Primary candidate: Mistral-Instruct-7B (good instruction-following, cost-efficient, strong multilingual base).
- Fallback / low-cost: MPT-7B-Instruct (fallback if we need a cheaper quantized instance).
- If higher quality needed: Llama-2-13B-chat (we can test but expect higher cost).

Ownership
- FinTech: Alex / Emma to provide sample dataset + success criteria sign-off.
- Redwood: Marissa (PM) to coordinate, Aditya for model setup/tuning, Neha for data security checklist and onboarding, Marcus for infra and region setup.

Next steps
1) Alex: confirm sample dataset size & any privacy redactions by Tue, Jun 22.
2) Redwood: share POC scope doc + evaluation template (attached).
3) Set kickoff call for Wed or Thu next week to confirm infra and test accounts.

Attachments: POC_scope.docx, evaluation_template.xlsx

Cheers,
Marissa Cole

Thanks, Alex — this looks good. Quick technical notes to set expectations for the POC model choices and infra: 

Model notes- Mistral-Instruct-7B: strong instruction-following and competitive token efficiency. Good first test for multilingual short queries. Recommend running it in an int8-quantized path (we've seen 2-3x throughput improvement with negligible quality loss for similar workloads).
- MPT-7B-Instruct (fallback): solid fallback for cost. On some domain-specific prompts MPT may be lower recall on entity extraction; we'll verify with the sample set.
- Llama-2-13B-chat: bring-up only if initial candidates underperform; expect ~2x token cost and higher latencies unless we use larger instance types.

Infrastructure & tuning- Region: US-west preferred for your traffic. We'll provision dedicated trial capacity (shared pool) and set autoscale caps for the test window.
- Caching: we'll enable prefix KV caching for replayed traffic to reduce cost for repeated queries (will not change quality metrics but lowers unit cost).
- Metrics: we'll instrument p95 latency, throughput, token counts, and token-level cost. Also collect human eval results via the evaluation_template.

Security / compliance- Neha will handle the SOC2 checklist and confirm that redaction approach meets our ingestion policy.

Requested items from FinTech- Final redacted sample by Tue EOD (Jun 23) if possible.
- Any specific prompt templates you want us to test (e.g. explicit system instructions for conservative answers).

Happy to run a short technical kickoff on Thu 11am PT (I can do that time).
